title: Extraction of Nuclei from Brain Tissue
author: Laura Bortolin
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.2srged6

steps.title: Retrieve chilled equipment
steps.instruction: Take the dissection tray from the -20 °C freezer, and retrieve the glass slide, razor blade, and ruler from the 4 °C refrigerator.

steps.title: Set up dissection workspace
steps.instruction: Place the glass slide, razor blade, and ruler on the dissection tray; keep the tray on ice to keep it cold and prevent movement while cutting.

steps.title: Trim frozen brain sample
steps.instruction: Put the frozen brain sample on the glass slide, shave off the frosty/freezer‑burned surface and discard it, then quickly shave off enough viable tissue for the extraction.

steps.title: Store trimmed tissue temporarily
steps.instruction: Return the shaved tissue to a -80 °C freezer (or place on dry ice if a short hold is needed).

steps.title: Mince tissue in extraction buffer
steps.instruction: Rapidly mince the shaved tissue with the same razor blade, scrape the minced pieces into the first well of a 6‑well plate containing 4 mL cold extraction buffer, and pipette the suspension up and down 20 times.

steps.title: Incubate homogenate with periodic pipetting
steps.instruction: Incubate the homogenate for 10 minutes at 4 °C, using a 1000 µL pipette to mix up and down 20 times approximately every 2.5 minutes.

steps.title: Transfer homogenate through 6‑well plate
steps.instruction: Using a chilled needle/syringe, draw the homogenate and expel it into the second well of the 6‑well plate; repeat with the same syringe to expel into the third well. Note that two distinct samples can be processed simultaneously in the top and bottom three wells.

substeps.instruction: Repeat pull and expel into third well.

steps.title: Filter homogenate through 20 µm filter
steps.instruction: Wet a 20 µm filter with 200 µL cold WB, pull the sample through the filter using gentle vacuum, then wash the filter with 2 mL cold WB while avoiding bubbles.

steps.title: Optional: Filter through 5 µm filter
steps.instruction: If desired, wet a 5 µm filter with 200 µL WB, pull the sample through using gentle vacuum, and wash with 2 mL cold WB. This step can be omitted for low‑debris samples or when preserving larger nuclei is critical.

steps.title: Optional: Baseline nuclei imaging
steps.instruction: Remove 10 µL of nuclei, mix with 10 mL diluted Hoechst stain, view on a fluorescent scope using brightfield and DAPI filters, and photograph both channels to confirm nuclei presence before proceeding.

steps.title: Dilute filtered nuclei to ~50 mL
steps.instruction: Add chilled WB to the filtered nuclei until the total volume is just under 50 mL.

steps.title: Aliquot nuclei into 50 mL tubes
steps.instruction: Divide the ~50 mL suspension into four 50 mL conical tubes, delivering approximately 14 mL per tube; avoid using 15 mL tubes because nuclei do not travel the longer distance well.

steps.title: Remove supernatant without disturbing pellet
steps.instruction: Carefully aspirate as much supernatant as possible from each tube without disturbing the invisible pellet.

steps.title: Resuspend pellet in WB and combine
steps.instruction: Resuspend each pellet in ~1 mL WB, then combine the four resuspended pellets; the final volume should be about 1.5–2 mL of extracted nuclei.

steps.title: Count nuclei and adjust concentration
steps.instruction: Obtain nuclei counts, calculate concentration, and dilute with DB to the desired concentration; for Nuclear Drop‑seq, dilute to 176 nuclei/µL.

steps.title: Stain nuclei for final imaging
steps.instruction: Mix 10 mL of the nuclei suspension with 10 mL diluted Hoechst stain, visualize on the fluorescent scope, and capture brightfield and DAPI images (debris should be less than in the baseline step).

steps.title: Spin nuclei at appropriate rcf
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the nuclei at 500 rcf for marmoset and human samples (600 rcf for mouse samples) for 10 minutes at 4 °C.
